title: The Man Who Feared His Shadow
summary: A man was running breathlessly through the village, screaming that a dark phantom was pursuing his footsteps....
keywords: the man who feared his shadow
full_text:
In the bustling Anatolian town of Akşehir, where donkey carts rattled through the spice bazaar and tea glasses clinked under the plane trees, lived Mulla Nasruddin. One afternoon, A man was running breathlessly through the village, screaming that a dark phantom was pursuing his footsteps..... The local folk, who never missed an opportunity to hear the Mulla’s unexpected pronouncements, quickly formed an expectant circle around him, stroking their beards and whispering among themselves.

Seeing everyone staring at him with grave expressions, Nasruddin adjusted his voluminous turban with theatrical dignity. A crowd of curious onlookers gathered in a circle, eagerly anticipating how the Mulla would resolve the impossible dilemma. Rather than offering a conventional, boring answer that any dry scholar might recite, the Mulla approached the problem from an angle that no one in the village had ever dreamed possible.

With effortless timing and a completely straight face, Nasruddin delivered his masterstroke: With deadpan gravity and a twinkle in his eye, Nasruddin delivered his unforgettable verdict.  The entire square erupted into bewildered chuckles and hearty laughter, leaving the bewildered questioners shaking their heads in admiration, proving that running from imaginary fears exhausts the runner; step into the shade of peace.
moral: Running from imaginary fears exhausts the runner; step into the shade of peace.
